settled-setup-before-m2:
## Setup Mirko must do before M2 (the loop will BLOCK on these otherwise)

**Decided 2026-07-24 (delegated to Claude): a dedicated disposable sandbox space on Moberg's own Confluence — NOT the existing `ITAPPS` space.** `publish --prune` deletes orphan pages and republish overwrites hand edits by design, so the loop must never point at a space holding human content or watchers. Full rationale and the accepted cross-tenant consequence: `.claude/references/decisions.md`. Only the clicks below are left; nothing here needs another judgement call.

- [x] **Create the space** on Moberg's Confluence. **Done 2026-07-26 (Mirko: "Space created").** Name `DocuMe Sandbox`, key `DOCUMESBX`, permissions restricted to Mirko so machine churn and machine comments never reach anyone's notification feed.
- [x] **Set the key:** **Done 2026-07-26 08:31** — `confluence.sandboxSpaceKey` is `"DOCUMESBX"` in `tools/loop/state.json`. **The key is assumed, not verified:** it is the value this checklist specified, set from an interactive session that has no Confluence credentials, so nothing has actually resolved it against the live space. A 404 on first lookup means the key is wrong — report the exact key tried and ask, do not guess another. A 401/403 means the token, not the key (see the API-token item below). Before the first write, sanity-check that the space is empty: the safety case for `publish --prune` rests on this being a dedicated disposable space.
- [x] **Set the sandbox base URL.** **Done 2026-07-25 21:07 (Mirko, mid-iteration):** `confluence.sandboxBaseUrl` is `https://moberg.atlassian.net/wiki`, which also confirms the sandbox tenant is `moberg.atlassian.net`. The sandbox is on a *different tenant* than production `AUR` (`kvika.atlassian.net`), and `state.json → confluence` had no field for this. *(Corrected iter66: no code change is needed to consume it. The tool has always taken a base URL — `confluence.baseUrl` in `docume.json`, required and validated at `src/DocuMe.Core/Config/ConfigLoader.cs:48`, written by `docume init --base-url`. This field is loop bookkeeping: it tells the loop which tenant to point the dogfood repo's `docume.json` at.)*
- [x] **Create an API token** for your *Moberg-site* account. **VERIFIED BY THE LOOP 2026-07-26 (iter112), not ticked by hand:** the credentials already exported in the loop's shell authenticate against `moberg.atlassian.net`. Evidence: a read-only `GET /wiki/api/v2/spaces?keys=DOCUMESBX` returned **200** (not 401/403), resolving `DOCUMESBX` to space id **451870722**. So the exported token is a Moberg-site token, not the Kvika/AUR one, and the cross-tenant worry recorded above is closed. Probe: `.mtk/paths-112/probe-space.py` (read-only, never writes, never logs the token).
- [x] **Export credentials, then RESTART the loop.** `DOCUME_CONFLUENCE_EMAIL` and `DOCUME_CONFLUENCE_TOKEN` must be exported in the shell that launches `tools/loop/docume-loop.sh`. **Done — verified 2026-07-25 (iter33):** the running loop has both vars. Evidence: a `docume publish` smoke run got past `ConfluenceCredentials.FromEnvironment()` (which throws when either is missing) and reached the space lookup. Which token/account it is has not been checked, and cannot be from inside the loop — if it is the Kvika/AUR token it will not work against a Moberg-site sandbox (cross-tenant), so the API-token item above may still be outstanding.

**NOTHING IS LEFT BLOCKING A LIVE SANDBOX RUN — all four setup items are done as of 2026-07-26 (iter112).** Space, key, base URL and token are all confirmed, the last of them by measurement rather than assumption (see the token item above).
